concepts.title: Sequencing Events in a Story
concepts.description: Learning to identify and arrange the order of events in a story using transition words like first, next, then, and finally.
key_ideas: Identifying the beginning, middle, and end of a story
Using sequence words (First, Next, Last)

concepts.title: Understanding New Words from Context
concepts.description: Using surrounding words, sentences, and illustrations to guess the meaning of unfamiliar vocabulary without using a dictionary.
key_ideas: Looking at the whole sentence for clues
Using pictures to understand difficult words
Identifying synonyms or antonyms within the text

concepts.title: Identifying Character Feelings and Traits
concepts.description: Analyzing what characters say and do to understand their emotions and personality traits.
key_ideas: Connecting actions to feelings (e.g., crying means sad)
Describing characters using adjectives (brave, kind, naughty)
Understanding how feelings change throughout a story

concepts.title: Finding the Main Idea
concepts.description: Determining the central topic or the most important point of a short paragraph or story.
key_ideas: Identifying what the story is mostly about
Using the title as a clue
Distinguishing the main idea from small details

concepts.title: Making Predictions
concepts.description: Using clues from the text and illustrations to guess what might happen next in a story.
key_ideas: Using current events to guess future outcomes
Looking at pictures to predict the story
Verifying predictions after reading

concepts.title: Nouns: Singular and Plural
concepts.description: Learn how to change words from one to many by adding 's' or 'es' to nouns.
key_ideas: Difference between one (singular) and many (plural)
Adding 's' to standard nouns
Adding 'es' to words ending in ch, sh, s, x, or z

concepts.title: Punctuation Marks
concepts.description: Understanding the basic marks used to start and end sentences correctly.
key_ideas: Using capital letters for the start of sentences and names
Using full stops (.) to end statements
Using question marks (?) for asking questions

concepts.title: Adjectives (Describing Words)
concepts.description: Identifying words that describe the quality, color, size, or number of nouns.

concepts.title: Prepositions (Position Words)
concepts.description: Using words that tell us where a person, animal, or thing is located.
key_ideas: Common position words: in, on, under, behind, near

Visualizing spatial relationships

concepts.title: Conjunctions (Joining Words)
concepts.description: Learning how to join two words or short sentences together to make longer sentences.
key_ideas: Using 'and' to join similar ideas
Using 'but' to show a difference or opposite idea
Using 'or' to show a choice

concepts.title: Picture Composition
concepts.description: Learn to observe a picture and write meaningful sentences describing the actions, objects, and setting shown in the image.
key_ideas: Observing visual details carefully
Using Present Continuous Tense (e.g., is playing, are sitting)
Connecting sentences to form a scene description

concepts.title: Story Completion
concepts.description: Develop the skill of writing short stories by using given outlines, clues, or filling in the blanks to complete a narrative.
key_ideas: Understanding the sequence of events (Beginning, Middle, End)
Using connecting words (First, Then, Finally)
Identifying the moral of the story

concepts.title: Describing People and Objects
concepts.description: Learn how to write a descriptive paragraph about a specific person, pet, or object using appropriate adjectives and sensory details.
key_ideas: Describing physical appearance (looks)
Describing qualities or personality (traits)
Using adjectives to make writing interesting

concepts.title: Writing a Leave Application
concepts.description: Understand the format and tone required to write a formal application to the Principal requesting sick leave or urgent leave.
key_ideas: Format of a formal application (Receiver's address, Date, Subject)
Formal salutations and polite language
Stating the reason for absence clearly

concepts.title: Synonyms
concepts.description: Synonyms — part of the chapter on Vocabulary.
key_ideas: Core principles of synonyms

concepts.title: Homophones — Words that Sound Alike
concepts.description: Homophones — Words that Sound Alike — part of the chapter on Vocabulary.
key_ideas: Core principles of homophones
Step-by-step problem solving for homophones

concepts.title: Antonyms — Words with Opposite Meanings
concepts.description: Introduction to words that have opposite meanings to one another, helping to expand descriptive capabilities and understanding of contrast.
key_ideas: Identifying opposites (e.g., hot/cold, happy/sad)
Using antonyms to change the meaning of a sentence
Common prefixes used to create antonyms (e.g., happy/unhappy)

concepts.title: Compound Words
concepts.description: Learning how to combine two smaller, distinct words to create a new word with a specific meaning.
key_ideas: Combining two nouns to form a new noun (e.g., sun + flower = sunflower)
Understanding that the new word's meaning relates to its parts
Identifying compound words in sentences

concepts.title: Collective Nouns
concepts.description: Vocabulary specific to naming groups of people, animals, or things as a single unit.
key_ideas: Specific terms for animal groups (e.g., a pride of lions, a flock of sheep)
Terms for groups of objects (e.g., a bunch of keys)
Using singular verbs with collective nouns

concepts.title: Introduction to Prefixes and Suffixes
concepts.description: Understanding how adding letters to the beginning (prefix) or end (suffix) of a root word changes its meaning or grammatical function.
key_ideas: Common prefixes (un-, dis-, re-) and their meanings
Common suffixes (-ful, -less, -ly) and their functions
Identifying root words within modified words

concepts.title: Using Context Clues
concepts.description: Developing the skill to guess the meaning of unfamiliar words by looking at the surrounding words and sentences.
key_ideas: Looking for synonyms or definitions in the sentence
Using antonyms as clues for meaning
Inferring meaning based on the general situation or story
